title: Dal Makhani
subtitle: Slow-cooked black lentil and kidney bean dal with butter and cream
excerpt: The great Punjabi dal: whole black lentils and red kidney beans slow-cooked overnight until utterly tender, then simmered for hours in a spiced tomato base with generous amounts of butter and cream until silky, deeply rich, and intensely savoury.

recipe.sourceNotes: Dal makhani (makhani means buttery) was created and popularised by Kundan Lal Gujral and his son Kundan Lal Jaggi, who opened Moti Mahal restaurant in Old Delhi in the late 1940s after partition. The restaurant's slow-cooked, tandoor-finished dishes (also the origin of butter chicken and dal bukhara) became famous and the recipes spread worldwide. Dal makhani uses whole urad dal (black gram lentils) which must be soaked overnight and cooked for at least 6 to 8 hours, originally overnight in a slow-burning tandoor. At home, a very low oven or slow cooker approximates this. The prolonged cooking breaks down the lentil skins and creates a creamy, unified texture that cannot be achieved quickly. The butter and cream are added at the end and are essential to the dish's character.

content.text: Soak the lentils and kidney beans overnight; they must be soaked before cooking or the lentils will never become fully tender. The longer the dal cooks, the better: 4 hours at a very gentle simmer is a minimum; 6 to 8 hours in a low oven or slow cooker is better. The dal should be so thick it holds its shape briefly on the spoon before slowly settling.

items.preparation: whole black lentils (urad dal) preferred; soaked overnight and drained
dried; soaked overnight with the lentils and drained

content.text: Drain the soaked lentils and kidney beans. Cover with fresh water in a large pot (at least 3:1 water to lentils). Bring to the boil and cook at a rolling boil for 10 minutes. Reduce to a low simmer and cook for 45 to 60 minutes until both are completely soft. Drain, reserving 500 ml of the cooking water.

Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 12 minutes until deep golden. Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the spices and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree and tinned tomatoes. Cook for 10 minutes until thick.

Add the cooked lentils and beans with the reserved cooking water. Stir well and season generously. Simmer over the lowest possible heat for at least 2 hours, stirring every 20 minutes, until the dal is thick, unified, and creamy. Add the butter and most of the cream and stir through. Taste and adjust salt. Serve with the remaining cream swirled on top, with basmati rice or naan.
